mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5, or Rank IC < 0.02 in any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and employment growth (PAYEMS) indicate manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both INDPRO and PAYEMS decline, or interaction Rank IC < 0.02 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) triggers expected monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5, or Rank IC < 0.02 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Residential construction permits below 1,200,000 units (HOUST < 1200.0) signal weak housing market conditions that reduce consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 1200.0, or Rank IC < 0.02 in any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real sales above $470 billion (RSAFS > 470000.0) indicates strong consumer demand that boosts corporate revenues, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS > 470000.0, or Rank IC < 0.02 in any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth exceeding 100,000 jobs (PAYEMS > 100.0) signals robust labor market conditions that increase consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS > 100.0, or Rank IC < 0.02 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1 < GDPC1[-1]) signals economic contraction that reduces corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 declines from prior quarter, or Rank IC < 0.02 in any 3-year rolling window.
